title: R' Yonatan of Habirah

paragraphs: R' Yonatan of Habirah. Hyman writes: It seems that he is the one called R' Yonatan ben Elazar of Habirah. And as in Midrash Tehillim 20:3: Rashbag went up from Babylonia to ask three things, and found Yonatan of Habirah. And Sefer HaDorot brings 'R' Yonatan, man of Kevurah' from this midrash, and the Tanchuma obscures the identification by saying that he happened to meet him. And in Aggadat Bereshit 8: Rashbag said, R'

Yonatan of Habirah. And likewise we find in Tanchuma, Bechukotai 4: Rashbag asked R' Yonatan ben Elazar, 'Teach me one chapter.' He said to him, 'Go to the house of study' — he said, 'Rabbi, did you not teach me?' etc. Hyman writes: From this we see that he was his student, and he is the unqualified R' Yonatan, the student of R' Chiyya who was Rashbag's teacher, as we brought that R' Yonatan was the student

of R' Shimon ben Lakonia. Hyman writes: And so we find that R' Yonatan ben Elazar was his student in Shabbat 49b, where R' Yonatan ben Elazar said to R' Yonatan ben Akhinai and to R' Chanina bar Chama: Thus said Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi Yose ben Lakonia. (And in Pesachim 51a, by error, R' Yochanan.) He is also mentioned by name, R' Yonatan ben Elazar, in Chagigah 20a regarding halakhah. And in Tanchuma Vayishlach 26, 'Beshalchah,'
and there, 'Hatzurdi': an incident of R' Yonatan ben Elazar who was sitting — and he called the students. And in Bereshit Rabbah 95:3, R' Yonatan 'sar habirah' is mentioned.

The whole consulted Buber Tanchuma Bechukotai 4 names Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman asking Rabbi Yonatan ben Elazar; its Townsend English says Johanan. The Torat Emet parallel is section 3 and names Shmuel bar Nachmani. The reply “Rabbi, did you not teach me?” is a question. Aggadat Bereshit 8:4 likewise has Shmuel bar Nachmani in the name of Yonatan of Habirah. These witnesses are compared with Hyman’s retained Rashbag siglum, without silently identifying or expanding it. A related whole Midrash Tehillim passage is at 3:3 in the consulted OYW text, beside Hyman’s supplied 20:3; it has the three questions and mixes Yochanan sar Habirah with later Yonatan. Hyman’s tentative identification and confident student inference remain his arguments, not an admitted genealogy. The whole Buber Beshalach 5 names Yonatan ben Elazar in the cedar-timbers parable, a comparison for supplied בשלחה; the exact הצורדי reference remains unresolved, and the consulted Buber Vayishlach 26 instead names Yonatan ben Ilai. Chagigah 20a names Yonatan ben Elazar locally; Bereshit Rabbah 95:3 has Yonatan sar Habirah. These names and titles are not merged. The full Shabbat 49b Shimon son of Yose ben Lakonia reading remains; Hyman’s alleged Pesachim error is not a newly collated printing.
